content:
My first research paper — and learning how to find my voice as a researcher.

As I embarked upon writing my first research paper, to be honest, I didn't have any idea where to start from. There were no answers to what was expected of me in terms of research, what topic should I choose, which authors should I engage with and how to structure my thoughts.

But gradually, I started figuring out the process.

I learnt how to choose a topic, identify the scholars that I would engage with, study their works and learn not only their arguments but also the context and life that informed their scholarship.

The topic that I chose was Partition — something I have personally felt close to since it was Punjab that bore the brunt of the Partition of 1947 and the after effects of this event can still be traced in the stories of displacement, separation and loss.

While exploring the theme of the gendered experience of Partition, I became interested in an issue that seemed rather underexplored to me:

How did patriarchy impact men during Partition?

While the experiences of violence, displacement and the social burden borne by women have been rightfully discussed, the experiences of men remained largely unexplored. I wanted to examine what kind of expectations society had for them in terms of masculine ideals of toughness, responsibility and protection, whether patriarchy was a benefit for them or it could have been a burden.

For me, writing my first research paper was about more than producing a good academic piece. I needed to learn how to do research and ask questions in order to finally form my own perspective on things.

It was a long and often lonely journey but immensely rewarding.

I am thankful to my supervisor, Dr. Maya Joshi who guided me through this long and rather overwhelming process, she showed me how to turn a very daunting beginning into something manageable. Constant encouragement and patience made me believe in myself and be ready to question my assumptions and trust the research process.

A big thank you to Saumya Yadav for helping me throughout my research journey. A special thanks to Anirudh Mittal for his constant encouragement, valuable suggestions and motivation throughout the project. Truly grateful for the support.

From this experience, I learnt a valuable lesson: sometimes, the hardest part of the research is figuring out how to start.
